title: Giant Prolactin-Secreting Pituitary Adenoma: A Case Report and Literature Review.
authors: Ocon Rodríguez JA, López Méndez A, Mondragón Rosas E, Arias Villaverde AA, Gloria Méndez E, Cruz Méndez M, Rivas Ayala L, González Flores JE.
figures: MRI demonstrating a giant invasive pituitary macroadenoma. Sagittal (a), coronal (b), and axial (c) T1-weighted post-contrast images reveal a large sellar and suprasellar mass with heterogeneous enhancement (circled in red). The tumor invades both cavernous sinuses, compresses the optic chiasm, and extends into adjacent structures

T1-weighted axial MRI showing a large, well-defined sellar and suprasellar mass (circled in red), consistent with an invasive pituitary macroadenoma. The lesion exerts a mass effect on the optic chiasm and extends laterally toward both cavernous sinuses
